summary: Confirmed NOT_DONE. Since f1be4abc7, nothing in Ryco or the Hub shortcuts the T_ADV wait. T_ADV is still the fixed 1_500. The initiator still arms advTimer at channel.accept, and for a legacy-eligible, legacy-permitted selection with no carrier, timer expiry is still the only path to lockLegacy (row K13). The engine still withholds onTransportStatus('online') and onOpen until #applyModeLock. The node still suppresses the carrier silently. The Hub forwards channel.accept as the node's original bytes and adds no marker. `git log -S` for T_ADV, advTimer and noCarrier only hits the report HTML embedded in #710. Two parts of the finding have changed. (1) The 'x2 per relay drop' multiplier is gone: a38ecac4b adopts the reconnected relay channel instead of rebuilding the client, so a relay drop now pays T_ADV once (1.5 s), not 3 s. (2) The 'undersized-connection' branch cannot happen against the production Hub, which asserts maxDataChunkBytes = 256 KiB, well above the 8,192-byte floor. The affected population is un-upgraded nodes plus nodes whose statement build fails. The cost also applies to apps/mobile legacy-eligible/permitted selections, not only web.

evidence.note: T_ADV = 1_500, unchanged; still documented as fixed by the L1 keepalive budget.

advTimer is armed at machine creation (channel.accept). On expiry with no hello: latched or !legacyPermitted gives P19, unexpected gives P22, otherwise lockLegacy() (K13). There is no hint input or early-lock path. This file has no commits since f1be4abc7.

channel.accept with an e2ee provider enters 'negotiating' and opens the machine. #applyModeLock flushes the negotiation buffer and only then emits onTransportStatus('online'), 'synchronizing' and onOpen. The engine changes since the report are buffer-ownership and copy-elimination only.

planFor returns 'suppress' for undersized-connection or statement-unavailable when requireE2EE is false. The suppress announce sends nothing on the wire and only records a node-local §12.5 occurrence.

RELAY_MAX_DATA_CHUNK_BYTES = 256 KiB, the value the Hub asserts in ready (ryco-hub origin/main src/relay/websocketRuntime.ts:785,925). That is above E2EE_ADVERTISEMENT_MIN_CHUNK_BYTES (8,192), so the 'undersized-connection' suppression is unreachable in production.
Web: selectionClass is 'latched' or 'legacy-eligible', with legacyPermitted: true. The only changes since the report are lazy-loading and warm-up of the handshake code.
Mobile also runs legacyPermitted from strictLegacyPolicy, which defaults to permitted, so mobile legacy-eligible first-contact selections pay the same K13 wait. The auditor covered web only.
The K13 test still pins mode 'negotiating' at T_ADV-1 and 'legacy' at T_ADV.
The spec still fixes T_ADV at 1,500 ms, and K13 is unamended. The 47 lines added to the spec since the report are §14.7 native fast paths and a §13.6 pending-record note, both unrelated.

channel.accept is forwarded with enqueueOriginal (node bytes verbatim) and gets no Hub-added marker. git grep finds no noCarrier or capability hint. ticketService.ts returns only {ticket, expiresAt, protocolMajor, protocolMinor} for non-account-grant tickets.

The Hub does receive node.e2ee.statement frames and acks them (Ryco HubConnector.ts:1159 notes the Hub drops a statement that is not renewed). The Hub therefore holds the 'node has a current statement' fact the proposal relies on, but no API exposes it.
Adopts the reconnected relay channel instead of rebuilding the client, removing finding #1's double establishment. A relay drop now pays T_ADV once rather than twice.

The web does label a legacy-locked channel ('legacy' status). What is missing is attributing the 1.5 s connect delay to 'node advertisement unavailable'. Only the node CLI shows the advertisement-unavailable counters (apps/server/src/cli.ts:2445-2474).

remaining: Every hosted connect and reconnect to a node that sends no E2EE carrier still waits a fixed 1.5 s before any RPC flows. Affected nodes are un-upgraded nodes and nodes whose statement build fails ('statement-unavailable'); 'undersized-connection' cannot happen against the 256 KiB production Hub. The client side is relayE2eeInitiator.ts:566-586 (K13 timer is the only legacy path), with sends held until relayEngine.ts:971-987. Applies to web (e2eeAttempt.ts:216-217) and to mobile legacy-eligible/permitted selections. The node suppresses silently (NodeE2eeChannelAdvertiser.ts:230,255-268). The Hub exposes no 'node has no current statement' signal: forwarder.ts:221 forwards accept verbatim, and the ticket response has no hint. Correction to the finding's cost: since a38ecac4b a relay drop costs 1.5 s, not 3 s.
implementationSketch:
Preferred: a Hub-originated hint on the ticket response, plus a K13 amendment.

1. Hub (ryco-hub)
- In src/e2ee/accountE2eeService.ts (acceptNodeStatement ~:791), track per node connection whether a current acked node.e2ee.statement exists. Clear the fact on statement expiry (non-renewal) and on node disconnect.
- In src/relay/ticketService.ts issueInternal, add `nodeE2eeAdvertisement: "absent"` to the plain ticket response only when the node's current connection has NEVER published a statement. That is the un-upgraded case and the persistent statement-build-failure case. Do not send it merely because a statement lapsed, so a stale hint cannot silently strip E2EE from an E2EE-capable node behind an honest Hub.
- Put the hint on the ticket response, not on channel.accept. The forwarder relays the node's accept bytes verbatim (enqueueOriginal), and adding a field there means re-encoding a node frame.

2. Ryco contracts
- Add the optional field to the ticket response schema in packages/contracts/src/relay.ts.
- Thread it through packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts into RelayE2eeInitiatorAttempt as e.g. `nodeAdvertisementHint?: "absent"`, set by the web/mobile attempt builders (apps/web/src/hostedHub/e2eeAttempt.ts:webRelayE2eeAttempt, apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/e2eeAttempt.ts).

3. Initiator (packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayE2eeInitiator.ts ~:566)
- Arm advTimer exactly as today.
- Lock legacy at creation only when the hint is 'absent' AND selectionClass === 'legacy-eligible' AND legacyPermitted AND !pairingOnly. Use lockLegacy(), which already goes through host.lockMode; the engine's #pendingLock handles a lock issued inside the factory (relayEngine.ts:955-959).
- Latched, unexpected, require-E2EE and pairing-only selections keep the timer and fail closed.
- A carrier arriving after the early lock is K20 (ignore, never upgrade). Record a diagnostic so a wrong hint is visible.

4. Spec
- Amend docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md §4.4: add a K13a row ('Hub hint absent' at accept, same guard as K13) and a §12.1.1 sentence stating the hint can only shorten the K13 wait for a selection already legacy-eligible and can never move a selection into that class.
- Get crypto/owner review.

5. Tests
- relayE2eeInitiator.test.ts: hint plus legacy-eligible gives mode 'legacy' and onOpen before T_ADV. Hint plus latched gives P19 at T_ADV. Hint plus pairingOnly gives fatal 'local'. Hint, then a carrier, gives K20 no-op.
- A transport test that the ticket field reaches the attempt.
- Hub ticketService tests for the field.

Cheaper client-only alternative (also a K13 amendment): keep an in-memory per (hubOrigin, accountId, nodeId) 'observed no carrier' bit in apps/web/src/hostedHub/e2eeAttempt.ts. Set it when a channel reaches K13 having seen no carrier at all. Clear it on any carrier (K1-K3, K20) and on page reload. On later channels, lock legacy at accept under the same guards. This removes the wait from reconnects but not from the first connect.

Node-only partial alternative, for upgraded-but-degraded nodes only: on 'suppress', emit a harmless legacy JSON record at seq 0 so the client takes K9 immediately. This needs node-row (N16/N17) spec changes, needs proof the RPC parser tolerates the record, and does nothing for un-upgraded nodes. Not recommended.

Independently, attribute the delay: when a channel locks via K13 with no carrier observed, publish a client-side diagnostic ('node did not advertise E2EE; connect waited 1.5 s') next to the existing 'legacy' label (apps/web/src/hostedHub/e2eeSession.ts:104).
decisionReason: Every fix changes §4.4 row K13 of the relay E2EE protocol, the only row besides K9 that releases plaintext. It lets a Hub-supplied hint, or a client-side negative latch, end the negotiation window early. That needs a spec amendment and a crypto/security review: showing that the hint grants no new downgrade power and that a stale hint cannot silently strip E2EE from a capable node behind an honest Hub. The preferred variant is also a Hub protocol change (a new ticket-response field) that needs a Hub deploy and a pin bump. The affected population (un-upgraded nodes, failed statement builds) shrinks as nodes update, so the trade-off between 1.5 s of latency and protocol complexity is a product decision.
correction: The auditor's classification and evidence hold. Gaps: (1) the finding's '-3 s per relay drop combined with finding #1' no longer applies, because a38ecac4b adopts the reconnected channel, so a drop now pays T_ADV once (1.5 s). (2) 'undersized-connection' suppression is unreachable against the production Hub (asserted 256 KiB vs the 8,192-byte floor), so the real population is un-upgraded nodes and statement-build failures. (3) mobile legacy-eligible/permitted selections pay the same wait (apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/e2eeAttempt.ts:590). (4) 'nothing is shown on the client' overstates it: the web labels the channel 'legacy' (e2eeSession.ts:104-106) but does not attribute the delay. (5) A Hub hint fits more naturally on the ticket response than on channel.accept, because the forwarder relays the node's accept bytes verbatim (forwarder.ts:221-227).
